title: Homeopathy’s COVID Cure Myth Busted
description:
Homeopathy has long sold itself as an alternative to science-based medicine, but what happens when even homeopaths admit their own remedies don’t work? In this episode, Pale Blue Thoughts revisits the infamous Arsenicum Album 30C (Ars Alb)—a sugar pill touted during the COVID-19 pandemic as an “immune booster” by the Ministry of AYUSH and widely consumed across India, especially Kerala. Supporters claimed it could prevent infection, boost recovery, and even act as a cure. But does the evidence support any of this?

We break down a randomized control study conducted by homeopaths themselves and published in their own journal, which tested 2294 participants across six groups, including Ars Alb, Bryonia Alba, Corona Virus Nosode CVN01 30C, and placebo. The results? Arsenicum Album—alone or in combination—showed no benefit whatsoever in preventing COVID or boosting immunity. In fact, the study inadvertently confirmed what skeptics had said all along: Ars Alb is just a placebo.

If you’ve searched for “Arsenicum Album 30C, homeopathy COVID cure, Ars Alb placebo, AYUSH pseudoscience, does homeopathy work”, this video gives you the scientific perspective. Supporters may still cling to anecdotes and conspiracy theories, but science has spoken—and ironically, even homeopaths provided the proof.

Homeopathy remains a pseudoscience rooted in 18th-century magical thinking, not modern biology. If you want real protection against infectious diseases, the answer lies in vaccines, public health measures, and evidence-based medicine—not sugar pills in fancy bottles. Don’t forget to like, share, comment, and subscribe for more myth-busting content.
